dataStructures.name: Linked List
dataStructures.summary: Linear collection of data elements where each node points to the next via a reference pointer.
keyInterviewInsights: Use Fast & Slow pointers (Floyd's Cycle Detection) to find middle node or detect loops in O(1) space.
Dummy head pointer simplifies boundary deletions and merges.
In-place reversal requires three pointers: prev, curr, and next.

dataStructures.name: Stack
dataStructures.summary: Last In, First Out (LIFO) collection where insertions and deletions happen only at the top.
keyInterviewInsights: Monotonic Stacks solve Next Greater Element, Daily Temperatures, and Largest Rectangle in Histogram in O(n).
Essential for expression evaluation, parenthesis matching, and DFS recursion call stacks.

dataStructures.name: Queue & Deque
dataStructures.summary: First In, First Out (FIFO) collection where elements are inserted at rear and removed from front.
keyInterviewInsights: Fundamental to Level-Order Tree Traversal and Breadth First Search (BFS).
Monotonic Deque solves Sliding Window Maximum in O(n) total time.

dataStructures.name: Binary Search Tree (BST)
dataStructures.summary: Binary tree where every node in left subtree is <= root, and every node in right subtree is >= root.
keyInterviewInsights: In-order traversal of a BST produces elements in strictly ascending sorted order.
Unbalanced BST degenerates to a linked list with O(n) operations; self-balancing trees guarantee O(log n).
Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) in BST can be found in O(h) without extra space.

dataStructures.name: Heap (Min-Heap / Max-Heap)
dataStructures.summary: Complete binary tree satisfying the heap property: parent is always <= (min-heap) or >= (max-heap) children.
keyInterviewInsights: Array indexing: Parent at (i-1)//2, Left child at 2i + 1, Right child at 2i + 2.
Building a heap takes O(n) time with bottom-up heapify (not O(n log n)).
Two Heaps pattern (Min-Heap + Max-Heap) maintains continuous Median of a data stream in O(1) peek and O(log n) insert.

dataStructures.name: Trie (Prefix Tree)
dataStructures.summary: Tree-like search data structure used to store dynamic strings where keys share common prefixes.
keyInterviewInsights: L is the length of the string, completely independent of the number of words stored in the dictionary.
Powers search engine autocomplete, spell checkers, IP routing lookups, and Boggle word search.

dataStructures.name: Segment Tree & Fenwick Tree
dataStructures.summary: Tree data structures storing intervals or prefix sums to support fast range queries and updates.
keyInterviewInsights: Fenwick Tree uses bitwise i += (i & -i) to achieve O(log n) point updates and prefix sum queries with minimal array memory.
Segment Tree supports arbitrary associative operations: Range Min, Range Max, Range GCD, Range Sum.

dataStructures.name: Graph (Adjacency List vs Matrix)
dataStructures.summary: Set of vertices V connected by edges E, representing complex relational networks.
keyInterviewInsights: Adjacency List is preferred for sparse graphs (O(V + E) space); Matrix is preferred for dense graphs (O(V^2)).
Topological Sort (Kahn's In-Degree Algorithm / Post-order DFS) solves dependency resolution and course scheduling.

coreAlgorithms.name: Quicksort
coreAlgorithms.summary: Partitions array around a pivot element so left <= pivot and right >= pivot, then recurses on subarrays.
coreAlgorithms.notes: Fastest practical in-memory sort due to cache locality. Randomized pivot or median-of-three prevents O(n²) worst case on sorted arrays.

coreAlgorithms.name: Mergesort
coreAlgorithms.summary: Divides array into two halves, recursively sorts them, and merges the two sorted subarrays.
coreAlgorithms.notes: Guaranteed O(n log n) in all cases. Stable sorting preserved. Preferred for sorting linked lists in O(1) auxiliary stack space.

coreAlgorithms.name: Depth First Search (DFS)
coreAlgorithms.summary: Explores as deep as possible along each branch before backtracking using a recursion stack.
coreAlgorithms.notes: Ideal for cycle detection, connected components, path finding, maze solving, and backtracking.

coreAlgorithms.name: Breadth First Search (BFS)
coreAlgorithms.summary: Visits all neighbors at the current depth level before moving deeper using a FIFO queue.
coreAlgorithms.notes: Guarantees the shortest path in unweighted graphs. Essential for level-order tree traversal.

coreAlgorithms.name: Topological Sort
coreAlgorithms.summary: Produces a linear ordering of vertices in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) such that for every edge u -> v, u comes before v.
coreAlgorithms.notes: Implemented via Kahn's algorithm (Queue of in-degree 0 nodes) or DFS. If processed node count < V, graph contains a cycle!
